flags: Sezzle and WebBank entered into a Second Amended and Restated Loan and Receivables Sale Agreement and Servicing Agreement, expanding the bank program to support SezzleCash and Sezzle Send, and increasing the minimum tangible net worth covenant from $12.0 million to $100.0 million.

Sezzle submitted an application to the OCC to charter a de novo national bank, Sezzle Bank, N.A., and an application to the FDIC for deposit insurance, and expects to apply to the Federal Reserve for bank holding company approval.

Sezzle reported Q3 2026 results (Total Revenue $166.5 million, Net Income $47.8 million) and raised FY2026 guidance for the fourth time to approximately 42.5% Total Revenue growth, $190.0 million Adjusted Net Income, and $5.45–$5.50 Adjusted Net Income per Diluted Share, while introducing preliminary FY2027 guidance of $7.20 Adjusted Net Income per Diluted Share.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K Business section (P1).
business_model.claim: Sezzle operates a digital shopping and payments platform that extends short-term consumer credit at the point of sale, with its flagship 'pay-in-four' product allowing consumers to pay in four installments over six weeks.
quotes: The Sezzle Platform offers a payments solution for consumers that instantly extends credit at the point-of-sale, allowing consumers to purchase and receive the ordered merchandise at the time of sale while paying in installments over time.

The Sezzle Platform flagship product, 'pay-in-four,' allows consumers to pay a fourth of the purchase price up front, and then another fourth of the purchase price every two weeks thereafter over a total of six weeks.

business_model.claim: Sezzle earns merchant processing fees, predominantly based on a percentage of GMV plus a fixed fee per transaction, and pays merchants the full transaction value upfront net of that fee, assuming all consumer credit risk.
quotes: We earn fees from our merchants predominately based on a percentage of the GMV value plus a fixed fee per transaction, collectively called a 'merchant processing fee.' We generally pay our merchants the full transaction value upfront, net of the merchant processing fee owed to us, and assume all costs associated with consumer payment processing, fraud, and payment default.
